chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of Umar ibn Musa, from their father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Dyeing (the hair) with vinegar cuts the desire for adultery.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of using vinegar for dyeing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of dyeing hair with vinegar (*khal*) to the spiritual discipline of curbing lust (*shahwa*), reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing bodily practices as means to purify the soul. This teaching underscores the holistic Islamic view where mundane acts, when performed with intention, serve as mechanisms for moral self-regulation and sexual chastity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary, from Muhammad and Ahmad the two sons of Umar Bin Musa, from their father, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The staining (of the food) with the vinegar cuts the desire of the adultery’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ibrahim al-Ja‘fariy from Muhammad and Ahmad sons of ‘Umar ibn Musa from their father in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Using vinegar as sauce cuts down the desire of fornication.’”
